weather_temp_series.png: Daily TEMP (degC) colored by meteorological season; red lines mark the 4 days dropped from the primary cloud (missing SLP). TEMP itself has no missing values in 2192 days.
weather_pca_panels.png: PCA (cumulative 97.6% variance in 2 PCs) of the z-scored TEMP/DEWP/SLP cloud. Left: seasonal organization. Right: ONI phase coloring is DESCRIPTIVE CONTEXT ONLY — no station-level ENSO hypothesis is tested; the 2019-2024 window holds roughly two ENSO episodes (power statement).
weather_mapper_reference.png: Reference Mapper graph (PCA-1 lens, n_cubes=10, overlap=0.35, KMeans k=2 seed=42): 20 nodes, 26 edges, 1 component(s), cyclomatic number 7. Node color = mean z-scored temperature of member days. Mapper graph cycles are not automatically topological loops (baseline no-loop control); note the cold-warm polarization along the graph.
weather_mapper_lens_comparison.png: Lens comparison at the reference cell: PCA-1 lens vs day-of-year lens (20 nodes, 27 edges, 1 comp). The day-of-year lens ENCODES calendar information directly — seasonal separation under it is partially built in and must be read beside the unsupervised PCA-lens result (left).
weather_mapper_grid.png: The pre-specified parameter grid on the weather cloud. Node count = 2 x n_cubes in all 8 cells (same uninformative pattern as baseline E2); the graph stays connected for n_cubes<=15 and fragments into 2 components at n_cubes=20 under both overlaps — the baseline E2 parameter-sensitivity finding replicates on real data.
weather_seasonal_ph_reference_barcode.pn: H1 barcode of the reference sliding-window embedding: one long bar (the dominant H1 class — consistent with recurrent seasonal or quasi-periodic structure in the embedded series, not proof of a simple closed physical climate trajectory) followed by short noise-scale classes. Custom renderer (persim ships diagrams, not barcodes — baseline E1 audit finding).
weather_seasonal_ph_reference_diagram.pn: Persistence diagram of the reference sliding-window embedding (tau=60 d, d=8, span 420 d, n=1772 points in R^8). One H1 class dominates (persistence 2.167 z-units, r_1=6.753); r_1>=3 is the stated convention, not a theorem. A dominant H1 class evidences recurrent quasi-periodic structure of the embedded series — NOT proof of a simple closed physical climate trajectory.
weather_seasonal_ph_sweep.png: Seasonal-cycle PH parameter sweep as a LABELLED SCATTER (Stage-3 revision: points are NOT connected — tau and embedding dimension d vary jointly across six discrete configurations; no smooth response surface is implied. Stage-4 revision: labels use leader lines with hand-placed anchors so that no two labels overlap). Every configuration yields one dominant H1 class (r_1 between 4.7 and 7.3, above the stated r_1 >= 3 convention) — consistent with recurrent seasonal or quasi-periodic structure in the embedded temperature series; this does not by itself prove a simple closed physical climate trajectory or independently validate an annual period (post-hoc sanity check: weather_seasonality_check.png). The sub-annual span is NOT a null control: any non-commensurate delay embedding of a periodic signal traces a closed curve; the negative representation contrast is the state-space cloud (weather_state_space_ph.png).
weather_state_space_ph.png: Vietoris-Rips PH of the 3-D z-scored daily state-space cloud itself: 1049 H1 classes, dominant persistence 0.2103, r_1=1.186 — NO dominant loop. The annual signal is a property of the TEMPORAL organization (recurrence in time, recovered by the sliding-window embedding), not of the static geometry of daily weather states, which weather variability fills in.
weather_state_space_ph_barcode.png: H1 barcode of the 3-D state-space cloud: no dominant bar — the visual counterpart of the state-space NEGATIVE REPRESENTATION CONTRAST (contrast with the seasonal barcode).
weather_embedding_pca.png: The 8-D reference sliding-window embedding projected to its first two PCA components: a closed band with a hole — the visual counterpart of the dominant H1 class. Colors follow the season of each window's start day and progress around the loop, as expected for an annual cycle. A 2-D projection of an 8-D embedding is a rendering, not the computed topology; the quantitative evidence is the persistence diagram.
weather_seasonality_check.png: POST-HOC SANITY CHECK (added at Stage 3; NOT used to select or retune any embedding parameter — the sweep was pre-specified and saved first): FFT periodogram and autocorrelation of the z-scored daily TEMP series itself. The series carries near-annual periodicity (dominant period 365 d; autocorrelation peak lag 360 d within the 180-550 d search window), consistent with the recurrent structure recovered by the sliding-window PH. This is a descriptive cross-check, not a hypothesis test.
